request.deadline: 12 months from deployment; month-6 yield distribution
deliverables: Sell deployed ADA for USDM to provide stablecoin-denominated liquidity for Strike Finance V2
Return realized yield from the first six months to the Cardano Treasury at month 6
Return 100% of treasury-owned deployed assets, including remaining principal and realized yield, at month 12

Provide monthly public transparency reports covering deployment status, utilization, volume, open interest, profit and loss, yield, drawdown, stablecoin exposure, market quality, distributions, and material risks
Provide third-party assurance reports at deployment confirmation, month 6, and month 12
request.recipient: Independent council administrator for Strike Finance liquidity deployment
request.what: 12-month productive treasury deployment into Strike Finance V2 liquidity infrastructure

claims.claim: The proposal requests 9,000,000 ADA for a 12-month liquidity deployment, not grant funding, with treasury ownership retained throughout deployment.
The deployed ADA will be sold for USDM, modeled at ADA = 0.15 USD to create approximately 1,350,000 USDM of liquidity.
Under modeled assumptions of a 10% USD-denominated APR, the deployment is expected to generate approximately 135,000 USD, or 900,000 ADA-equivalent, in annual yield, but returns are not guaranteed.

Strike reports more than 1.13 billion USD in cumulative volume, roughly 968,000 to 1,001,000 trades, more than 3,000 unique traders, over 1.16 million USD in protocol revenue, and over 3.25 million USD in liquidity provider profit.
Strike V2 data from 2026-03-20 through 2026-06-15 is presented as showing 87,288,044 USD total V2 volume, 410,800 total V2 trades, 2,681 total V2 users, and 30,105 USD total V2 revenue.

The proposal says Strike's liquidity provider vault has 985,271.59 USD TVL, 43.52% APR, +8.85% all-time return, 1.15% maximum drawdown, and 208 depositors after two months of public performance history.

Operational custody would be handled by an independent multisig council composed of Rami from Snek, Phil from Surf, and James from Monetra, and Strike Finance would not have unilateral custody or control of treasury assets.

The proposal identifies primary risks including ADA appreciation underperformance versus holding ADA, USDM depeg or redemption risk, smart contract risk, yield underperformance, liquidity risk, and custody or operational risk.

Governance review is triggered if drawdown exceeds 8%, reporting is missed for two consecutive monthly cycles, or unresolved custody, accounting, stablecoin, redemption, or smart contract concerns arise, with mandatory review at 10% drawdown and a separate wind-down review at 20% drawdown.
The proposal states that an official audit by Christian Schmitz is expected to be finalized by July 1, 2026 and published upon completion.

summary: The document describes a large temporary treasury-owned liquidity deployment into Strike Finance V2, with modeled yield, multisig custody, reporting and assurance commitments, stated adoption metrics, and explicit market, stablecoin, smart-contract, and custody risks.
